name: Arkansas

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act (Ark. Code 17-16-101 and following, amended by Act 204 of 2011)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract covers endorsement deals (Ark. Code 17-16-102), and the NIL law says anyone who represents an athlete must hold the Arkansas license (Ark. Code 4-75-1305).
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $500, good for 2 years.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Application for Registration

steps.detail: Payable to the Secretary of State. It's $100 if you hold another state's registration or send another state's application from the last 6 months.

steps.text: Send the application and fee to the Secretary of State
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: If you contact an enrolled athlete by accident, tell the athletic director within 72 hours of the contact.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, any other pay you get, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the Warning to Student-Athlete box next to their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words below, in bold capital letters.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, if that comes first. This applies to a spoken agreement too. The athlete must tell the athletic director as well.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days
steps.detail: They cancel by written notice. They owe you nothing and keep anything you gave them to sign.

steps.text: Report each NIL deal to the school the way it asks
steps.detail: Tell the school's chosen official about your role and the deal's terms, parties and pay. The school sets the deadline.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law (SPARTA) bans pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of clients, every contract and what you spent recruiting each athlete.

steps.text: Never give gifts or money to recruit athletes or make false promises
steps.detail: Don't give anything of value before they sign, or to anyone but the athlete or another registered agent. Never pre-date or post-date a contract.
A registration lasts 2 years. It's $100 if you renew based on another state's renewal.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Statute text was read on Justia's 2024 and 2025 Arkansas Code, not the official Lexis code. Confirm on the Arkansas Code before launch.
Ark. Code 17-16-113 (records) was read on a secondary site because Justia failed to load. Confirm the 5-year rule on the official code.
Penalties (Ark. Code 17-16-115 and 17-16-117) were not reviewed in full. Act 204 of 2011 makes some violations a felony.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
